chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The witnesses must not refuse to answer when they are summoned, before the writing (of the contract).

key_terms.الشهداء: Witnesses — those present at and cognizant of a transaction or event, obligated to testify
key_terms.الكتاب: The writing/documentation — refers to the formal written record of a contract or debt, as mentioned in Quran 2:282
key_terms.يأب: To refuse/decline — implies a sinful or impermissible act of avoidance

ai.seo_question: Are witnesses obligated to respond when summoned in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a legal directive that witnesses to a contract or transaction are obligated to respond when called upon to testify, even before the formal documentation has been completed. This ruling addresses the civic duty of witnesses in Islamic jurisprudence — in the context of Quranic injunctions on contracts and testimony (2:282), the obligation to appear when summoned was understood as a communal and legal duty that witnesses could not evade.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The witnesses should not refuse to answer when they are summoned before the writing (documenting)’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Witnesses must not refuse to present their testimony when they are called before it (the case and testimony) is written down.’”
